A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-Critique method and RL-MIA benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original contamination-detection experiments, a dual-stage contamination study and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices B-D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama, UltraFeedback, prompt-sensitivity and bootstrap results in Tables 6, 8, 9 and 12.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same deterministic initial and conditioned critique generations, token-level entropy calculation, zero-padding and length-penalized cosine score. The additional model evaluations and prompt ablations do not revise the proposed detector.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds UltraFeedback evaluation under an RLHF alignment scenario, substantially extending coverage beyond v1's mathematical and logical reasoning contamination experiments. The original AIME24, AIME25, K&K, SAT and GSM8K coverage remains.

E2.justification: The evaluated detector set remains PPL, Min-K%, Min-K%++, Recall, CDD, Entropy-Temp and Entropy-Noise. The new Llama and UltraFeedback comparisons use this same set. PPO, DPO, TDPO and RTO describe target-model training conditions, not additional competing detectors.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on K&K/SAT and Llama-3-8B-Instruct trained using PPO, DPO, TDPO and RTO on UltraFeedback. Appendix C.3 also introduces an original-plus-five-variants prompt evaluation. Existing metrics, dataset splits and training hyperparameters are retained; these additions do not establish reruns or changed settings for the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct test of sensitivity to meta-instruction wording on AIME25 and K&K (Appendix C.3, Table 9), and extends algorithm-robustness evidence to four RLHF alignment procedures (Appendix B.3). The original initial-response, sampling-strategy, Top-K and dual-stage analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's point estimates and across-K variance, v2 introduces 1,000-resample bootstrap means, standard deviations and 95% confidence intervals for SAT across both main models and all detectors (Table 12). Table 9 also reports means and standard deviations across prompt templates. These quantify resampling and template variability, not additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: Matched original results remain unchanged, but substantial new results are reported. Table 6 gives Self-Critique AUCs of 0.61 and 0.62 on Llama-3.1 K&K and SAT. Table 8 reports 0.62, 0.62, 0.64 and 0.70 under PPO, DPO, TDPO and RTO, respectively. Tables 9 and 12 add prompt-variant results and bootstrap summaries. These are additional findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The membership-inference definition, training-objective equations, entropy definition and penalized cosine formulation are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: a first systematic study of RL contamination detection, the Self-Critique detector, RL-MIA and the headline AUC improvements. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 extends the policy-collapse interpretation across reward and alignment types, while C.3 attributes prompt stability to the underlying mechanism. New Appendix G explains baseline variability through random-prefix effects, interprets bootstrap uncertainty and argues for favorable inference-cost tradeoffs. The original limitations are relocated from G to H without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds the exact text of five paraphrased meta-instructions used in the new sensitivity study. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, data-split documentation and code/data access information remain unchanged. The added RLHF experiment references another work's setup without supplying detailed local splits and training configurations.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references for Llama, UltraFeedback, PPO, DPO, TDPO, RTO and bootstrap estimation. PPO attribution changes from Havrilla et al. to Schulman et al. The related-work narrative and principal novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v2 adds acknowledgements, appendix contents and new appendix subsections, expands existing appendix passages, and updates the publication header. There is no extensive rewrite. The reproducibility statement introduces incorrect references to Tables 6 and 7 for Appendix F, whose relevant tables are now 10 and 11.

P2.justification: The appendix gains dedicated displays for Llama performance, RLHF comparisons, prompt sensitivity and bootstrap uncertainty (Tables 6, 8, 9 and 12), plus five additional prompt panels and a contents page. These substantially expand the displayed evidence. Existing figures are retained, with a label correction in Figure 2 and relocation or reflow of appendix material.

improvement.justification: The added model/alignment evaluations, prompt checks and bootstrap intervals strengthen evidence for transfer and stability beyond v1. The benefit is limited by sparse setup documentation for the new RLHF experiment and interpretations stronger than the analyses establish. For example, Table 12's DeepSeek intervals for Self-Critique [0.55, 0.77] and PPL [0.52, 0.75] overlap; these marginal intervals alone do not establish the broad superiority suggested in Appendix G.1. Overall, the additions provide useful but qualified improvements in evidential support.
